description:
Track all your AI coding subscription usage from the Windows system tray.

OpenTokenUsage is a lightweight system-tray app that tracks how much of your AI coding subscriptions you've used (Claude, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini, and more) in one place. It is a Windows fork of OpenUsage with full Windows support, a plugin-based provider system, and a local HTTP usage API.
Two new providers, your live Claude Code sessions, usage by hour, your own alert levels per provider, costs in your currency, and settings you can take to another PC.
New Features
- OpenRouter and DeepSeek are new providers, off until you turn them on. Each reads its API key from a user environment variable (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY). OpenRouter shows the account's credits (when the key may read them), the key's spending cap with its reset, and the key's spend today and this month. DeepSeek shows the account balance (#65)
- Claude and Codex detail pages show when in the week you use them: tokens per weekday and hour over the last 4 weeks, with the busiest hour, read from the CLIs' own logs on this PC (#66)
- Claude cards list the Claude Code sessions running on this PC and what each one is doing. With the status line on, they also show how full each session's context is and warn before Claude Code compacts it (#59, #67)
- Claude Code status line (Settings): Claude Code can hand its 5-hour and weekly usage to the app. The Claude card then asks Anthropic far less often and keeps showing usage during a rate limit. It's off by default and never replaces a status line of your own (#55)
- Notifications: each provider can have its own alert levels, and the bars show a notch at each level (#58)
- Tray: with the percent style, "Color by pace" colors the number like the card's pace dot: green, yellow or red (#60)
- Usage mode: "Weekly pace on work days" counts a weekly window's pace from Monday to Friday only, so a quiet weekend no longer looks like room to spare (#61)
- Currency: show costs in one of 13 currencies at a rate you enter. No exchange-rate service is contacted (#62)
- Settings backup: export your preferences to a file and import them on another PC. Logins and accounts aren't included, and the other PC keeps its own extra accounts and custom sound (#63)
- Claude and Codex cards show the prompt cache hit rate of the last 30 days (#57)
- A card that asks you to sign in refreshes the moment the CLI signs in again, instead of at the next refresh. A sign-in lost while the app runs is notified once (#56)
Changes
- Claude: after a rate limit (HTTP 429), the app waits what Anthropic asks, but at least 5, 10, 20 and then 30 minutes for each rate limit in a row, until a read succeeds (#55)
